correctness.rationale: Independently reduced the unit-gap constraint on the class-constant mean-zero subspace using coordinates (peripheral value minus hub, pendant minus hub). The energy slack has diagonal k(a−2/(k+2)), c−(k+1)/(k+2) and off-diagonal k/(k+2); its PSD condition gives exactly a>2/(k+2), c≥c(a). The transverse modes require a+kb≥1. Permutation averaging preserves cost and cannot lower the gap. Positive prices force the lower bounds on b,c in the reduced optimum. On each side of a=1 the cost has positive second derivative, and the kink is upward. The left and right slopes there are kP−R/k−(k−1)Q/2 and kP−R/k. I checked the two stationary-point cost formulas by symbolic substitution, and the slopes give both stated threshold equalities, including a=c=1 and b=0 at R=k²P. For unrestricted uniqueness the quotient unit eigenvector of the average retains its Rayleigh energy under any optimum. Its nonzero edge differences force every hub rate; then either b=0 by nonnegativity or the peripheral compression has lower bound I and trace k−1, forcing equal peripheral weights. Budget scaling is exact by homogeneity.
residual_risks: The supplied numerical minimizations are finite and do not by themselves verify optimality or uniqueness; no formal proof-assistant claim is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These methods make the problem solvable but provide neither this price-dependent optimum nor its equality/rigidity conditions. A tree-only solution on the star support would not certify when deletion of all peripheral edges is optimal in the allowed clique.

evidence: The earlier PSD certificate has squared lengths equal to one on both hub-adjacent classes; a common cost multiplier cannot yield independent spoke and pendant prices. It has a transverse unit-gap eigenspace, whereas the expensive-pendant branch has a>1 and no transverse unit-gap mode.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: New boundary/equality analysis is required; a parameter renaming or specialization of the earlier certificate/theorem does not yield all phases.

originality.rationale: Pass for the full independent-price phase diagram and rigidity, not for the equal-price pendant/spoke slice. The prior pendant-clique result is a genuine theorem-level overlap, but its two-price theorem is not sufficient for the new competing branch at R>k²P, nor for its transition and unrestricted uniqueness over the independent three-price space. The general convex program and symmetry method are established prior work.
residual_risks: A specialized weighted-connectivity solution outside these checks could overlap; no exhaustive priority claim.
The frozen prior-work discussion omits the verified R=P predecessor, which should be credited in any public account.

value.rationale: Independent edge prices are natural for budgeted diffusion. The theorem tells when an entire edge class should be dropped, separates the two distinct zero-peripheral-rate behaviors, and certifies uniqueness over individual edge rates even at the boundaries. These are useful exact design facts beyond the known equal-price slice or a numerical SDP solution.
residual_risks: Restricted to one pendant and orbit-constant prices; no claim for more general networks or objectives.
